O.outcome_detail: QNC Level I basic numerical competencies

cells.quote: Importantly, and confirming our isolated number-words hypothesis, phonological awareness had no impact on higher numerical competencies (i.e., when number words had to be linked with quantities; QNC Level II and above), but predicted basic numerical competencies (i.e., when number words were isolated from quantities; QNC Level I), which explained the moderate relationship between early literacy development and the development of mathematical competencies.
cells.note: The study reports a positive prediction of QNC Level I, but the abstract does not provide a printed effect size for this association.

cells.quote: QNC Level I accounted for about 18% of the variance in subsequent QNC Level II/III ( = .42, p < .01), which in turn predicted about 32% of the differences in mathematical achievement in Grade 3 ( = .57, p < .05).
cells.note: This specific result is reported in the wiki entry; the supplied study text does not include the corresponding results section.

O.outcome_detail: higher numerical competencies, QNC Level II and above

cells.quote: Importantly, and confirming our isolated number-words hypothesis, phonological awareness had no impact on higher numerical competencies (i.e., when number words had to be linked with quantities; QNC Level II and above), but predicted basic numerical competencies (i.e., when number words were isolated from quantities; QNC Level I), which explained the moderate relationship between early literacy development and the development of mathematical competencies.
cells.note: The study reports no impact, but does not report an equivalence test or adequate power; therefore the direction is coded ns rather than 0.
